- Lauren/Alex: visibility for any manager/escalation approvals.

Target: please respond with your recommendation by EOD Tue 2/10 so I can decide whether to keep this in the Feb commit or move to next month.

Folks,

Attached is a short deal desk brief (deal_brief.xlsx) with comps and recommended concession structure. TL;DR: customer is mid-market, first close, referenceable, and committed to a 12-month term. Suggested path:
- Approve a 25% commercial discount (with standard support terms) — rationale: preserves unit economics and keeps deal within sales manager approval threshold.
- If Sales insists on 35%, require CFO approval + finance sign-off on ARR recognition caveats.

Impact to forecast (high level): at 35% the expected first-year ARR goes from $420,000 to ~$273,000 (net new). That would flip this from a "Commit" to "Commit at Risk" in our current forecast guidance unless we secure CFO approval prior to EOD close.

Please advise on internal approval process — I can route through Lauren then Markus if needed.

-rishi

Marissa / team,

From a finance perspective: any discount above 30% needs explicit CFO (or delegated) approval before we count the full ARR in our monthly commit. If we post the deal as a full Commit without that approval, we'll need to restate the forecast.

I modeled the impact quickly (attached pricing_impact_model.csv):
- List ARR: $420,000
- Proposed 35% discount: Net ARR $273,000 (Delta: -$147,000)
- Suggested compromise (25%): Net ARR $315,000 (Delta: -$105,000)

Recommendation for forecasting: mark the deal as "Commit (pending discount approval)" for the Feb rollup and include a separate line item in the "Pricing Exceptions" section. If we receive CFO approval before Feb month close we can promote to full Commit.

If Sales wants to push for 35% today, provide written CFO approval and updated revenue recognition assumptions; finance will then accept the full Commit but will annotate the ledger.

-Vivek
